source: verified live on 2026-09-18: each official or fred_oecd_10y entry returned a dated observation to python/refresh_rates.py before it was recorded here
notes: Tiers: official (issuer or central bank, machine-readable) > fred_oecd_10y (OECD monthly 10y via FRED; the 7y is taken from the 10y and recorded as a substitution) > manual (hand-copied; the 45-day gate forces the refresh).
Aggregators (worldgovernmentbonds, tradingeconomics) are never a programmatic source; they are where a human reads a manual entry from.
A failed fetch writes nothing; the existing entry stays and ages out.

Nothing fetched is tracked (29): the curves themselves are written by python/refresh_rates.py to data/reference/risk_free_rates.json, gitignored, and every user runs the refresher with their own FRED key; a missing curve fails the record naming the refresher. max_age_days, tenors and aliases here seed that file.

no_curve_fallback (54): a domicile named here has no reachable official curve, and a record whose statements and price are both in one currency takes that currency's country curve for the risk-free rate while keeping the domicile's country risk premium, the risk-free parameter's source saying "trading currency; domicile curve unavailable". Uruguay is the only entry: MercadoLibre files a 10-K in dollars and trades in dollars, so the dollar curve is the rate its cash flows discount at, and no Uruguayan sovereign curve is published through any keyless source. The list is a declaration, not a fallback: a domicile not named here still fails with no risk-free curve, and a domicile named here that does have a curve takes it.

Moved from the manual tier on 2026-10-03: the series answered python/refresh_rates.py with a dated observation before this entry was written. It is a monthly average that reaches FRED about two months after the month ends, so on most days it is older than the 45-day gate and an Indian-rupee record is refused for a stale rate, naming this refresher; that is the honest state of a source that slow, and no hand copy stands in for it. China.source: ChinaBond (China Central Depository & Clearing), the China Government Bond yield curve published at yield.chinabond.com.cn, read from the chart's own endpoint
notes: The endpoint answers a form POST (locale=en_US) and nothing to a GET, with the latest day's curve as (years, per cent) pairs on a grid that carries every whole-year tenor; the curve is picked by its id, which names the China Government Bond curve (中债国债收益率曲线); verified 2026-09-30, a dated curve came back to python/refresh_rates.py before this entry was written.
as_of is the day the curve is for (worktime), a daily observation.
FRED carries no OECD series for China.

Singapore.source: Monetary Authority of Singapore, Daily SGS Prices: closing yields of the benchmark Singapore Government Securities, read from MAS's own statistics page
notes: The page renders the closing-levels table server-side and keyless: the benchmark tenors, a row saying which cells are prices and which yields, and one dated row per business day; the newest row is the observation. Verified 2026-09-30, a dated observation came back to python/refresh_rates.py before this entry was written.

MAS's API gateway serves the same yields to a registered corporate account only, and its portal is closed to a foreign individual (a corporate email is required and the country of origin is fixed to Singapore), which is why the page and not the gateway is the source.

The benchmarks are 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 and 50 years; there is no 7-year benchmark, so the seven-year is substituted from the ten-year and recorded, as the OECD monthly tier does, and the three-year is not listed rather than taken from either neighbour.
as_of is the closing date the row carries, a daily observation.

Reading the page is permitted by MAS's own Terms of Use (mas.gov.sg/terms-of-use), which carry an Open Data Licence for the datasets MAS publishes: use, access, download, copy, distribute and adapt, commercially or not, on condition of a conspicuous notice acknowledging the source, with no restriction to Singapore residents or corporations; the corporate-account requirement gates the API gateway as a service, not the data. The source string on this entry and on every record's risk-free parameter is that notice; nothing fetched is redistributed. The page itself states that the yields reflect bid rates quoted by SGS primary dealers.

Hong Kong.source: HKGB Closing Reference Pricings, the Government of the Hong Kong SAR the owner: the daily closing yields of the benchmark institutional Government Bonds, from the Government Bond Programme's own workbook
notes: The workbook is published keyless on hkgb.gov.hk each business day: a benchmark sheet naming the tenors over a price and a yield column each and one dated row per day. Verified 2026-09-30, a dated observation came back to python/refresh_rates.py before this entry was written. It is a binary Excel file, the one such source in the registry, read with xlrd.

The benchmarks are one, three, five, seven, ten, fifteen and twenty years; the one-year is a HONIA-indexed floating rate note quoted at par with no yield, so the one-year is not listed rather than taken from the three-year. The seven-year is a benchmark of its own, so nothing is substituted.

The sheet's own terms: the figures are calculated each business day by Bloomberg from the Primary Dealers' quotes and published by the Government, which asks users to refer to them as HKGB Closing Reference Pricings and to quote the Government as their owner, which the source string on this entry and on every record's risk-free parameter does; nothing fetched is redistributed.

The HKMA open API was probed 2026-09-29 and serves Exchange Fund Bills and Notes closing yields to three years and the Government Bond Programme's issuance, outstanding and tender datasets, no bond yields; the workbook is where the yields are.

Denmark.source: Danmarks Nationalbank, ten-year central government bond redemption yield (monthly average), served keyless through Statistics Denmark's StatBank, table MPK3, series type 5500701004
notes: Danmarks Nationalbank's own StatBank states that its subject areas are served as part of Statistics Denmark's StatBank, which is why the host is api.statbank.dk and no Nationalbank host is used; verified 2026-09-24, a dated observation came back before this entry was written.

MPK3 carries no tenor shorter than ten years and the Nationalbank's daily table DNRENTD carries policy and reference rates only, not bond yields, so the seven-year is substituted from the ten-year and recorded, as the OECD monthly tier does.
as_of is the end of the observation month, the point at which the monthly average is complete.
The time filter is an open lower bound well in the past, so the URL never needs editing; the parser takes the newest period the response carries.
